All input fields
FieldTypeMeaning
queriesarrayOne Instahyre search per item, matched against job titles and skill tags, e.g. python, react, data science, devops, product management, java developer. Put cities in locations. A job found by two keywords is saved and charged once. Leave the list with one item for a quick first run.
allJobsbooleanIgnore the keywords and deliver every open Instahyre job: a full-board export for job aggregators and tech-hiring trackers (12,724 open jobs on 26 Oct 2026). Instahyre has no date filter, so combine it with Only new jobs since the last run: the first run exports the board and later runs open only the jobs they have not delivered. locations, company size, job type and maxJobs still apply; the per-keyword cap does not. You can also put * in the keywords.
locationsarrayOptional. Cities as Instahyre lists them: Bangalore, Mumbai, Delhi, Gurgaon, Noida, Hyderabad, Chennai, Pune, Kolkata, Ahmedabad, or Work From Home for remote roles; regions such as South India and about 300 smaller cities also work. Several cities = any of them. Common alternative spellings (Bengaluru, Gurugram, Bombay, Remote) are mapped; an unknown name is ignored with a note in the status message. Leave empty for all of India.
minExperienceintegerOnly jobs whose stated experience range reaches at least this many years (0-30). Checked on each job page; jobs that state no range are kept.
maxExperienceintegerOnly jobs whose stated experience range starts at or below this many years (0-30). 1 or 2 is a good early-career filter.
experienceYearsintegerInstahyre's own experience filter: only jobs open to a candidate with exactly this many years (the job's range must cover it). Applied by the site before anything is fetched, so it is the cheapest way to narrow a search; combine with minExperience/maxExperience for a band.
postedWithinDaysintegerOnly jobs posted in the last N days (1-365). Instahyre keeps jobs open for months and its search has no date filter, so the Actor reads the posting date from each job page and leaves out older jobs without charging. In only-new mode the jobs that are left out are remembered too, so later runs do not re-check them.
companySizesarrayOptional. Any of small (under 100 employees), medium (100-1,000) and large (over 1,000). Several values = any of them. Applied by the site.
jobTypestringall (default), full-time or internship. Applied by the site.
companiesarrayOptional. Only jobs posted by these companies, e.g. Amazon, Deutsche Telekom Digital Labs. Several names = any of them. Applied by the site; combine with an empty keyword list to watch everything a company posts.
includeDescriptionbooleanOn (default): one extra request per job reads the public job page and adds the full description (HTML and plain text), posting date, experience range, employment type, job functions and the company website. The price per job is the same either way. Off: listing fields only (title, company profile, cities, skills, URL), about three times as fast, enough for counting jobs or sizing a market.
maxJobsPerQueryintegerStop a keyword after this many new jobs (default 50). Cost: $0.0008 per job with its description, so 50 jobs = $0.04. Raise it for full exports: python alone matches about 4,300 open jobs and the site serves 35 per page.
maxJobsintegerHard cap on saved jobs for the whole run across all keywords (0 = no cap).
onlyNewSinceLastRunbooleanOn: deliver only jobs that an earlier run with the same stateName has not already delivered, and skip the rest without charging. Set maxJobsPerQuery high enough for the first run to take the whole result list (or add postedWithinDays), so later runs really return only new postings. Off (default): return every matching job.
stateNamestringOptional name for this search's memory when onlyNewSinceLastRun is on, e.g. python-bangalore-daily. Leave empty to derive it from the keywords, cities and filters. Use a new name to start over.
skipJobIdsarrayArray of job IDs you already have (the id field from earlier runs), e.g. ["424473", "441980"]. They are skipped before any page fetch and never charged. Large arrays are fine.

Price
$0.0008 per job ($0.80 per 1,000); $0.001 per run. List prices for Apify Free and Starter plans; Scale and Business plans pay 15% to 30% less.
EventPricePer 1,000Charged when
Job$0.0008$0.80One job with its full description: title, company profile, experience range, skills, functions, locations, posted date, job URL.
Actor Start$0.001Charged when the Actor starts running. Number of events charged depends on Actor memory (one event per GB, minimum one event).
Cost example: 50 jobs with default options cost $0.041, including any start fee. This is an illustrative record count; set explicit row and total-charge caps for your run. Apify's free plan includes $5 of usage a month, about 6,250 jobs before start fees; the Actor's own compute is included in the per-record price, and records skipped by filters, de-duplication or only-new mode are not charged.

What it is not for
Non-tech roles (IIMJobs, Foundit); salary bands (Instahyre does not publish pay); applicant counts (Hirist, IIMJobs). The data belongs to its publisher; the Actor reads public pages and endpoints and leaves out personal contact details.

Cyber security jobs in India (Instahyre): Cyber security, information security, SOC and cloud security roles open on Instahyre at Indian startups and product companies, with the full job description, posting date, experience range, skills, company size and websi {"queries": ["cyber security", "information security", "security engineer"], "includeDescription": true, "maxJobsPerQuery": 40}

Questions buyers ask
Is there an official Instahyre API?
No public one. This Actor reads the JSON that the Instahyre website itself loads for its job search, plus the public job pages, and exposes them as a REST API with schedules, webhooks and only-new-jobs runs. Compared with an in-house scraper you get no maintenance, no proxies and pay-per-job pricing.
How much does it cost to scrape Instahyre?
$0.0008 per job with its full description plus $0.001 per run, so 100 jobs cost about $0.08 and a 50-jobs-a-day feed about $1.25 a month.
Is it legal to scrape Instahyre?
The Actor only reads job pages and search results that Instahyre shows without a login, and it does not output recruiter names or look up e-mail addresses. Public job data is generally collected for aggregation, research and recruiting; you remain responsible for complying with Instahyre's terms of use and the data-protection law that applies to you.
Does it include recruiter emails, salaries or applicant counts?
No. Instahyre does not publish salary ranges or applicant counts on public job pages, and this Actor only reads public data and deliberately leaves out recruiter contact details.
Can I export Instahyre jobs to Excel or Google Sheets?
Yes. Every run's dataset downloads as CSV, Excel, JSON, XML or HTML, and the task's Integrations tab appends rows to a Google Sheet after each run.
Does it return the full job description?
Yes, as HTML and plain text, plus the experience range, posting date, job functions, skills and the company profile with headcount, founding year and website.
Why is the posting date old on many jobs?
Instahyre keeps a job open until the employer closes it, so a feed without postedWithinDays includes jobs posted months ago (the 30 Oct 2026 default run returned posting dates from March 2022 to the same day). Use postedWithinDays for recent postings, or only-new mode, which after the first run delivers only jobs that are new on the site.
Why does a city return nothing?
The site only accepts the location names it lists; the Actor maps the common alternative spellings and names any location it had to ignore in the status message. Use Bangalore, Delhi, Gurgaon, Noida, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Chennai, Pune, Kolkata, Ahmedabad or Work From Home.

Alternatives, honestly
OptionWhat it gives youWhere it falls short for this job
Instahyre websiteCandidate and employer accountsNo export or API; salary and applicant counts are not shown publicly anywhere
Hirist or IIMJobs APIs (same publisher)Applicant counts and salary bandsDifferent boards; Instahyre is the one with company headcount and size filters
Other Instahyre Actors on Apify StoreSame boardCompare price per 1,000, company-profile fields and only-new mode

Published by Daemon Data (data_daemon on Apify Store). Prices, fields and example pages read from the live Apify listing on 2026-11-06; the listing is the canonical description of the Actor.

Luma (lu.ma) events as JSON API

Luma Events Scraper & API is a pay-per-record Apify Actor by Daemon Data that returns lu.ma events by city, category, keyword or calendar: dates, venue, tickets, hosts as JSON, CSV or Excel. Daemon Data Luma Events Scraper & API on Apify   Listing as plain text

Checked on 19 Oct 2026, on the Apify platform
San Francisco listed 105 upcoming events; three cities (San Francisco, New York, London) gave 100 events with full details in 36 seconds for $0.15 plus the $0.001 start fee. The default run (the 25 soonest San Francisco events with details) takes about 10 seconds and costs $0.04.

Example input. Fields and pricing were checked against the public listing on 2026-11-06; this build does not run paid example searches.

{
  "cities": [
    "London"
  ],
  "categories": [
    "ai"
  ],
  "daysAhead": 30,
  "includeDetails": true,
  "maxEvents": 50
}

One HTTP call starts a run, waits for it and returns the records (token from console.apify.com):

curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/data_daemon~luma-events-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"cities": ["London"], "categories": ["ai"], "daysAhead": 30, "includeDetails": true, "maxEvents": 50}'

Python: ApifyClient(token).actor("data_daemon/luma-events-scraper").call(run_input=...). Python example · Node.js example · n8n workflow.

All input fields
FieldTypeMeaning
citiesarrayLuma discover cities, e.g. San Francisco, New York, London, Berlin, Bengaluru, Tokyo, Singapore (87 cities; a lu.ma/<city> URL or a discplace-... id works too). One upcoming-events feed per city, newest start date last. An event found in two feeds is saved and charged once. Leave one city for a quick first run; set the list empty to search worldwide with a keyword.
categoriesarrayOptional. Luma categories: ai, tech, arts, climate, crypto, fitness, wellness, running, books, games, family, fooddrink. Each category is scraped around each city above (Luma lists category events by location). Several categories = any of them.
querystringOptional keyword searched by Luma in event names and descriptions, e.g. hackathon, founders, yoga, web3. Applied inside each city, category and calendar feed (Luma returns the 50 best matches per feed). With cities set to an empty list and no other source, it searches worldwide.
startUrlsarrayOptional. Any public lu.ma / luma.com link: an organiser calendar (https://lu.ma/planetscale), a single event (https://lu.ma/qjw9i5a9), a city (https://lu.ma/sf) or a category (https://lu.ma/ai); cal-..., evt-..., discplace-... ids too. Calendars return their upcoming events. When only URLs are given, the default city is not scraped.
daysAheadintegerOnly events starting within the next N days (1-365), e.g. 7 for this week's events. Leave empty for all upcoming events (feeds are ordered by start date, so maxEvents takes the soonest ones).
startDateFromstringOptional earliest start date, YYYY-MM-DD or ISO date-time (UTC), e.g. 2026-11-01. Applied by Luma's own date cursor, so later pages are not fetched for nothing.
startDateTostringOptional latest start date, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive) or ISO date-time. Each feed stops at the first event after this date.
priceTypestringany (default), free (ticket price 0 / no ticket) or paid (at least one paid ticket type). Checked on every event before it is saved or charged.
eventFormatstringany (default), in-person (events with a physical venue) or online (no venue or a meeting link as the venue, incl. events whose location is not announced).
includeDetailsbooleanOn (default): one extra request per new event adds the full description (plain text and HTML), every public ticket type with its price, the event's Luma categories and the sold-out flag. The price per event is the same either way. Off: feed fields only (name, dates, venue, GPS, price range, hosts, calendar, guest count), roughly twice as fast.
maxEventsintegerStop after this many saved events (default 25). Cost: $0.0015 per event with details, so 25 events = $0.04. A city has 50-150 upcoming events; raise this for full exports.
maxEventsPerSourceintegerOptional cap per feed so one busy city does not use up maxEvents (0 = no cap).
onlyNewSinceLastRunbooleanOn: deliver only events that an earlier run with the same stateName has not already delivered, and skip the rest without charging. Off (default): return every matching event.
stateNamestringOptional name for this search's memory when onlyNewSinceLastRun is on, e.g. sf-ai-daily. Leave empty to derive it from the cities, categories, keyword and URLs. Use a new key to start over.
skipEventIdsarrayEvent ids you already have (the id field from earlier runs, e.g. evt-Dgnnl0IoUmK5Se1; lu.ma/<slug> URLs are accepted too). Skipped before any detail fetch and never charged. Large lists are fine.

Price
$0.0015 per event ($1.50 per 1,000); $0.001 per run. List prices for Apify Free and Starter plans; Scale and Business plans pay 15% to 30% less.
EventPricePer 1,000Charged when
Event$0.0015$1.50One Luma event saved to the dataset: id, URL, name, start/end (UTC + local + timezone), in-person/online, venue, address, city, region, country, GPS, free/paid, price range and currency, sold-out, spots remaining, approval, guest count, organiser calendar (name, URL, website, socials), hosts (name, bio, profile URL, website, LinkedIn/X/Instagram handles), categories, cover image, full description (text + HTML) and ticket types. Details included in the price; skipped or filtered events are never charged.
Actor Start$0.001Charged when the Actor starts running. Number of events charged depends on Actor memory (one event per GB, minimum one event).
Cost example: 50 events with default options cost $0.076, including any start fee. This is an illustrative record count; set explicit row and total-charge caps for your run. Apify's free plan includes $5 of usage a month, about 3,333 events before start fees; the Actor's own compute is included in the per-record price, and records skipped by filters, de-duplication or only-new mode are not charged.

What it is not for
Eventbrite, Meetup (not covered); attendee or guest lists (never collected). The data belongs to its publisher; the Actor reads public pages and endpoints and leaves out personal contact details.

Ready-made example pages
Saved inputs you can run with one click on Apify (Examples tab); each has its own page:
Tech events in San Francisco this week (Luma): Every Luma (lu.ma) Tech-category event in and around San Francisco starting in the next 7 days, with venue, GPS, prices, hosts, organiser calendar and full description. Save it as your own task and schedule it weekly. {"cities": ["San Francisco"], "categories": ["tech"], "daysAhead": 7, "maxEvents": 100}
AI events in London - next 30 days (Luma): Upcoming Luma (lu.ma) AI events in and around London over the next 30 days: meetups, hackathons, talks and workshops with venue, GPS, free/paid, hosts with LinkedIn/X handles and full descriptions. {"cities": ["London"], "categories": ["ai"], "daysAhead": 30, "maxEvents": 100}
Startup & tech events in Bengaluru (Bangalore) - Luma: Upcoming Luma (lu.ma) Tech and AI events in Bengaluru (Bangalore): founder meetups, demo days, hackathons and builder nights with venue, GPS, prices, hosts and organiser calendars. {"cities": ["Bengaluru"], "categories": ["tech", "ai"], "maxEvents": 100}
Luma (lu.ma) events in New York, next 14 days, as JSON: Upcoming public events on Luma in New York over the next two weeks with date, venue, hosts, ticket types and prices, as JSON or CSV. Change the city or add categories such as ai, tech or crypto. {"cities": ["New York"], "daysAhead": 14, "includeDetails": true, "maxEvents": 50}

Questions buyers ask
How much does it cost to scrape Luma?
$0.0015 per event with its full details plus $0.001 per run, so 100 events cost about $0.15 and a daily feed of 20 new events about $1 a month.
Is there an official Luma API?
Luma has a paid API for calendar owners (their own events). This Actor reads the public JSON that the lu.ma website itself loads for discover, category, calendar and event pages, and exposes it as a REST API with schedules, webhooks and only-new runs. No login or API key is needed.
Does it collect attendees or guest lists?
No. The Actor never requests or outputs guest lists, guest names, e-mails or phone numbers, including the "N going" avatars shown on event pages. It outputs the hosts' and organiser calendar's public profile information exactly as the event page shows it (name, bio, profile URL, website and social handles).
Why is the address missing on some events?
Hosts can show the exact address only to registered guests. Luma then shows the city and neighbourhood, and so does the Actor: address and venue are null, addressHidden is true, and the coordinates are rounded to about 1 km. City, region and country are still filled in.
Why does an online-only run of a city return nothing?
Luma's city and category pages list events with a physical location near that city. Online events are found through organiser calendars (startUrls) and keyword searches with cities: [], and are marked format: "online".
Which cities and categories exist?
The 87 cities on lu.ma/discover (any lu.ma/<city> page; the Actor also resolves new cities live) and the 12 categories ai, tech, arts, climate, crypto, fitness, wellness, running, books, games, family, fooddrink. A city or category Luma does not know ends the run with Saved 0 events and the known examples in the status message.
Can I scrape past events?
Not in this version: Luma's public feeds list upcoming events. Open an issue if you need an organiser's past events.
Does it work for luma.com links?
Yes. lu.ma and luma.com are the same site; paste either form in startUrls.

Alternatives, honestly
OptionWhat it gives youWhere it falls short for this job
Luma website and iCal feedsBrowse; subscribe to one calendarNo cross-city export, no host profiles in bulk
Eventbrite or Meetup ActorsOther event platformsDifferent events; this API reads Luma only
Other Luma Actors on Apify StoreSame sourceCompare detail fields (hosts, tickets, GPS) and price per 1,000

Published by Daemon Data (data_daemon on Apify Store). Prices, fields and example pages read from the live Apify listing on 2026-11-06; the listing is the canonical description of the Actor.

All input fields
FieldTypeMeaning
citiesarrayCity names as Magicbricks spells them, e.g. Mumbai, Pune, Bangalore (Bengaluru works too), Hyderabad, New Delhi, Gurgaon, Noida, Chennai, Kolkata, Ahmedabad. Each city is its own search; an unknown name is reported, not replaced.
transactionTypestringsale or rent (monthly rent in priceInr).
propertyTypesarrayapartment, builder floor, penthouse, studio, house, villa. Empty = all residential types in one search; with types chosen, each type is its own search (more listings per city).
minPriceintegerSale price or monthly rent; applied by Magicbricks' own budget filter.
maxPriceintegerSale price or monthly rent; applied by Magicbricks' own budget filter.
minBedroomsintegerKeep listings with at least this many bedrooms.
postedWithinDaysintegerKeep listings posted in the last N days (postedAt). 1 uses Magicbricks' own "posted in the last 24 hours" filter (fast). Magicbricks applies it with a lag: on 1 Nov 2026 it returned listings 34-43 hours old, so expect roughly the last two days; add only-new mode for a daily feed without repeats. Longer windows are checked on each listing, and a search stops after two pages of older listings.
maxResultsPerSearchintegerCap per city (and property type). 0 = no cap; Magicbricks lists at most 1,500 listings per search.
maxResultsintegerStop after this many saved listings (default 50, about $0.05). 0 = no cap.
onlyNewSinceLastRunbooleanRemember delivered listing ids in a key-value store named magicbricks-state and skip them next time (not charged).
stateNamestringBy default it follows cities, sale/rent and property types.
skipIdsarrayMagicbricks listing ids you already have. Not saved, not charged.

Price
$0.001 per listing ($1.00 per 1,000); $0.001 per run. List prices for Apify Free and Starter plans; Scale and Business plans pay 15% to 30% less.

FieldTypeMeaning
queriesarrayJob titles, skills or company names, one search each (e.g. data analyst, java developer, Infosys). Leave empty and turn on All jobs to export the whole board.

keywordInTitlebooleanKeep only jobs whose title contains every word of the keyword (e.g. data analyst keeps "Senior Data Analyst", drops "Business Analyst"). Left-out jobs are not charged. Off by default.
includeDescriptionbooleanOn (default): opens each job for the full description, applicants, views, role, function, industry, education, employment type and the company's website and address, at no extra charge. maxJobsintegerStop the run after this many jobs in total. 0 = no limit (the run's maximum cost still applies).
onlyNewSinceLastRunbooleanOn: deliver only jobs that an earlier run with the same stateName (or the same search) has not delivered, and skip the rest without charging. If postedWithinDays is empty it is set to 3. Off (default): return every matching job.
stateNamestringOptional name for the only-new memory, e.g. bangalore-data-jobs. Runs with the same name share one memory. Empty = derived from the keywords, cities, experience and work mode.
skipJobIdsarrayNaukri job IDs you already have (the id field, e.g. 041126017601); they are skipped and not charged.

Checked on 18 Oct 2026
Open jobs on verified career sites: Kotak Mahindra Bank 16,521, Marriott International 13,286, JPMorgan Chase 7,262, EXL Service 2,841, Oracle 2,372, DTCC 452. On 21 Oct 2026 one run read Oracle's and Marriott's sites together and returned 80 jobs posted in the last 7 days in 15 seconds.

Job boards and aggregatorsEnterprise employers that only post on their own Oracle site, with stable requisition IDs, posted dates and direct apply URLs. One run can walk many tenants.
Talent-intelligence and recruiting teamsTrack competitors' hiring by job family, function, country and city, and get only the new requisitions every day with Only new jobs since the last run.
B2B sales (hiring signals)A bank opening 40 data-engineering roles in Bengaluru is a buying signal. Get it the morning it posts.
Workforce and labour-market researchersHiring trends at Fortune-500-scale employers, including full JD text for skills extraction.
AI agents (MCP)"What remote engineering roles did JPMorgan Chase post this week?" Connect https://mcp.apify.com/?tools=data_daemon/oracle-hcm-jobs-scraper in Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor.

Input and how to call it

Example input. Fields and pricing were checked against the public listing on 2026-11-06; this build does not run paid example searches.

{
  "careerSiteUrls": [
    "https://eeho.fa.us2.oraclecloud.com/hcmUI/CandidateExperience/en/sites/CX_45001/requisitions"
  ],
  "keyword": "engineer",
  "postedWithinDays": 30,
  "includeDetails": true,
  "maxJobsPerSite": 50
}

One HTTP call starts a run, waits for it and returns the records (token from console.apify.com):

curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/data_daemon~oracle-hcm-jobs-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"careerSiteUrls": ["https://eeho.fa.us2.oraclecloud.com/hcmUI/CandidateExperience/en/sites/CX_45001/requisitions"], "keyword": "engineer", "postedWithinDays": 30, "includeDetails": true, "maxJobsPerSite": 50}'

Python: ApifyClient(token).actor("data_daemon/oracle-hcm-jobs-scraper").call(run_input=...). Python example · Node.js example · n8n workflow.
AI assistant (MCP): add the remote server https://mcp.apify.com/?tools=data_daemon/oracle-hcm-jobs-scraper with header Authorization: Bearer YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN in Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or VS Code and ask for the data in plain words.

All input fields
FieldTypeMeaning
careerSiteUrlsarrayOne or more Oracle Recruiting Cloud (Oracle HCM) career site URLs. They look like https://{tenant}.fa.{region}.oraclecloud.com/hcmUI/CandidateExperience/en/sites/{siteNumber}; any page of the site works, including a single job URL. Example: JPMorgan Chase = https://jpmc.fa.oraclecloud.com/hcmUI/CandidateExperience/en/sites/CX_1001. To find a company's site, web-search: site:oraclecloud.com CandidateExperience "". Taleo and Workday sites are not supported.
keywordstringOptional. Searched the way the career site's own search box does, e.g. data, nurse, sales manager. Leave empty to export every open job.
locationstringOptional country, state or city, e.g. India, United Kingdom, London, Bengaluru, Karnataka, India. Countries always work. States and cities are resolved through the site's own location filter; if the site does not list the place, jobs are matched on their location text instead and only matching jobs are delivered and charged. The run log lists the locations a site offers.
postedWithinDaysintegerOnly jobs posted recently. Integer 1-30; Oracle supports two buckets, so 1-7 means the last 7 days and 8-30 the last 30 days. Leave empty for all open jobs.
workplaceTypesarrayOptional: only remote, hybrid or on-site jobs. Works only on career sites that tag workplace type; some tag every job on-site (Oracle's own site does), and then Remote returns 0 jobs.
includeDetailsbooleanOn (default): full description, qualifications, responsibilities, skills and the employer's custom fields. No extra charge since 2 November 2026. Off: list fields only, faster.
maxJobsPerSiteintegerStop after this many jobs per career site (default 50, about $0.20 with details at FREE prices). Set 0 to export the whole site; large employers list 2,000-13,000 open jobs.
onlyNewSinceLastRunbooleanDeliver only jobs that an earlier run with the same search (or the same State key) has not already delivered. Skipped jobs are not charged. Made for daily schedules: the Actor remembers delivered job IDs in a key-value store named oracle-hcm-jobs-state in your account. When this is on and Posted within is empty, the last 7 days are searched.
stateNamestringOptional name for this saved search's memory when Only new jobs is on, e.g. jpmc-india. Leave empty to derive it from the career site URLs, keyword, location and workplace types. Use a new key to start over.
skipJobIdsarrayOptional requisition IDs to leave out, e.g. the id values from an earlier run. Skipped jobs are not charged. Large lists are fine.
maxJobsintegerHard cap for the whole run across all sites (0 = no cap).

Price
$0.002 per job ($2.00 per 1,000); $0.001 per run. List prices for Apify Free and Starter plans; Scale and Business plans pay 15% to 30% less.
EventPricePer 1,000Charged when

Actor Start$0.001Charged when the Actor starts running. Number of events charged depends on Actor memory (one event per GB, minimum one event).
Cost example: 50 jobs with default options cost $0.101, including any start fee. This is an illustrative record count; set explicit row and total-charge caps for your run. Apify's free plan includes $5 of usage a month, about 2,500 jobs before start fees; the Actor's own compute is included in the per-record price, and records skipped by filters, de-duplication or only-new mode are not charged.

What it is not for
Workday, Taleo, Greenhouse, Lever, SuccessFactors sites. The data belongs to its publisher; the Actor reads public pages and endpoints and leaves out personal contact details.

Questions buyers ask
How much does it cost to scrape an Oracle career site?
$0.002 per job with its full detail record, plus $0.001 per run. A 500-job site with details costs about $1.00.
Does Oracle Recruiting Cloud have a public API for job postings?
The documented Oracle HCM REST API needs customer credentials. Public career sites load their jobs from an unauthenticated candidate-experience endpoint (/hcmRestApi/resources/latest/recruitingCEJobRequisitions), which is what this Actor reads, with the same filters the careers page uses. The three endpoints, their parameters and the silent wrong-site fallback are documented in Oracle Recruiting Cloud jobs API: the public JSON endpoints behind every Oracle HCM career site.
What is the difference between Oracle HCM, Oracle Fusion and Oracle Recruiting Cloud?
Oracle Fusion Cloud HCM is the suite. Oracle Recruiting Cloud (ORC) is its recruiting module. The public careers page is called Candidate Experience, which is why the URLs contain CandidateExperience.
Does it read Taleo or Workday sites?
No. Taleo is Oracle's older, separate ATS and Workday is a different vendor. This Actor covers Oracle Recruiting Cloud (oraclecloud.com/hcmUI/CandidateExperience) sites only. Other hosts are skipped with a warning, not an error.
Why do I see several sites (CX_1, CX_1001, CX_45001) for one employer?
Tenants keep backup, campus and alumni sites. Use the one in the table above, or the one your browser shows on the employer's careers page. Oracle's own retired CX_1 still answers, but the live site is CX_45001.
Can I filter by city?
Yes. Cities and states are matched against the site's own location filter (for example LONDON, United Kingdom on JPMorgan Chase or Dubai, United Arab Emirates on Marriott). If a site only lists states, as Kotak does, the Actor matches the city against each job's location text instead, and only matching jobs are charged.
Which companies use Oracle Cloud HCM career sites?
Thousands of large employers: banks, hospitals, universities, manufacturers, retailers, hotel groups and governments. Their career pages live under oraclecloud.com/hcmUI/CandidateExperience/.
Do I need a proxy or login?
No.

Alternatives, honestly
OptionWhat it gives youWhere it falls short for this job
The employer's own career siteBrowse and applyOne employer at a time, no export
Multi-ATS job APIs (Workday, Greenhouse, Lever and others)Several ATS platforms in one productUsually higher price per 1,000; check whether Oracle Recruiting Cloud is actually covered
Open-source ATS crawlersFreeYou host, schedule and maintain them

# Shine.com job listings as JSON API | Daemon Data

Source: https://datadmon.github.io/actors/shine-jobs-scraper/

Shine.com job listings as JSON API

Shine Jobs Scraper is a pay-per-record Apify Actor by Daemon Data that returns Shine.com India jobs by keyword and city with full descriptions, salary range, experience, skills and industry as JSON, CSV or Excel. It costs $0.0008 per job with the default options ($0.80 per 1,000); no login to the source site and no proxy or browser to set up on your side, and the same input runs from the Apify console, one REST call, Python, Node.js, n8n or an AI assistant through MCP.

Daemon Data Shine Jobs Scraper on Apify   Listing as plain text

Checked on 30 Oct 2026
the default run (50 newest python jobs with descriptions) took 23 seconds on the Apify platform and cost $0.04 plus the $0.001 start fee. All 50 had a description, 19 showed a salary range, every posting was 1-3 days old, and the cities were Pune 18, Bangalore 17, Hyderabad 16, Chennai 7. On 26 Oct 2026, data analyst in Bangalore and Pune with 2 years of experience, posted in the last 3 days, gave 20 jobs from the first few pages (98 others were older, elsewhere or for another experience band, and were not charged).

Recruiters and staffing agenciesWho is hiring accountants in Mumbai or Java developers in Pune this week, at what salary and experience.

All input fields
FieldTypeMeaning
searchTermsarrayJob titles or skills, one Shine search each, e.g. python, data analyst, accountant, sales executive, java developer, nurse. Leave empty to list all jobs (in the given cities, or in India). A job found by two searches is saved and charged once.
citiesarrayCities as Shine names them, e.g. Bangalore, Mumbai, Delhi, Gurgaon, Noida, Hyderabad, Pune, Chennai, Kolkata, Ahmedabad, Navi Mumbai. Each keyword runs once per city. Shine also suggests jobs in nearby cities; the Actor keeps only jobs located in the city you asked for.
experienceYearsintegerOnly jobs whose experience range covers this many years, e.g. 2 keeps "1 to 3 Yrs" and "0 to 4 Yrs" but not "5 to 8 Yrs".
postedWithinDaysintegerOnly jobs posted in the last N days (e.g. 1 for a daily feed). Results are read newest first, so the search stops at the first page of older jobs. 0 or empty = any date.
includeDescriptionbooleanOpen each job page for the full description (text + HTML), numeric salary range, industry, function, employment type and expiry date. Turn off for a fast list of titles, companies, cities, experience, salary text and skills. Price is the same either way.
maxJobsPerSearchintegerCap for each keyword (and city). Newest jobs come first. 0 = no cap (a popular keyword can have tens of thousands of jobs; set a maximum cost per run).
maxJobsintegerStop after this many saved jobs. 0 or empty = no total cap (the run's maximum cost still applies).
onlyNewSinceLastRunbooleanFor schedules: remember delivered job ids (in a named key-value store in your account) and save only jobs that earlier runs with the same settings did not deliver. Skipped jobs are not charged.
stateNamestringName of the only-new memory. Empty = derived from the keywords, cities and experience. Give two schedules the same name to share one memory.
skipJobIdsarrayShine job ids you already have (the id field). They are neither fetched, saved nor charged.

Price
$0.0008 per job ($0.80 per 1,000); $0.001 per run. List prices for Apify Free and Starter plans; Scale and Business plans pay 15% to 30% less.

Questions buyers ask
Is there an official Shine API?
Not a public one. This Actor reads Shine's public search and job pages, which robots.txt allows, and exposes them as a REST API with schedules, webhooks and only-new runs. Compared with an in-house scraper you get no maintenance, no proxies and pay-per-job pricing.
How much does it cost to scrape Shine.com?
$0.0008 per job with its description plus $0.001 per run, so 100 jobs cost about $0.08 and a 40-jobs-a-day feed about $1 a month.
Is it legal to scrape Shine.com?
The Actor only reads listings that Shine shows to anyone without a login, on pages its robots.txt allows, and it does not extract recruiter names, phone numbers or e-mail fields. Public job data is generally collected for aggregation, research and recruiting; you remain responsible for complying with Shine's terms of use and the data-protection law that applies to you.
Can I export Shine jobs to Excel or Google Sheets?
Yes. Every run's dataset downloads as CSV, Excel, JSON, XML or HTML, and the task's Integrations tab appends rows to a Google Sheet after each run.
Does it include recruiter contact details?
No. Some Shine scrapers sell recruiter e-mails and phone numbers; this Actor deliberately leaves personal contact fields out and returns the job, employer, salary and description data only.
Why do some jobs have no salary numbers?
The employer chose "Not Disclosed". salaryText then says so.
Do I need a proxy?
No. If Shine starts refusing direct requests, the Actor switches to Apify's anti-bot proxy by itself.

# NSE/BSE stock fundamentals API (Tickertape) | Daemon Data

Source: https://datadmon.github.io/actors/tickertape-stocks-scraper/

NSE/BSE stock fundamentals API (Tickertape)

Indian Stock Market API is a pay-per-record Apify Actor by Daemon Data that returns NSE/BSE index constituents, ratio screener, full stock profiles as JSON, CSV or Excel. It costs $0.02 per stock profile with the default options ($20.00 per 1,000); no login to the source site and no proxy or browser to set up on your side, and the same input runs from the Apify console, one REST call, Python, Node.js, n8n or an AI assistant through MCP.

Daemon Data Indian Stock Market API on Apify   Listing as plain text

Checked on 18 Oct 2026
Tickertape listed 77 indices; a NIFTY 500 constituent run returns 500 rows for $1, and a full profile carries 10 years of statements plus the shareholding history. On 21 Oct 2026 five full profiles (Reliance, TCS, Infosys, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank) took 17 seconds.

Why teams use it
The whole stock page in one record. Statement lines come with readable names (Total Revenue, Net Income, EPS, Free Cash Flow), not just codes.
Shareholding as a trend. Six quarters of promoter, pledged, FII, DII, MF, insurance and retail percentages: compare quarters to spot FII exits or rising promoter pledges.
Screener plus enrichment. Filter on market cap, P/E, P/B, dividend yield, ROE, ROCE, debt/equity, 1-week to 1-year returns, beta, promoter pledge and FII/DII holding, then pull the full profile for every match in the same run.
Never a failed run on a typo. An unknown index name, a stock that does not exist or a screener with no matches finishes successfully with 0 rows and a status message that says why, so schedules and webhooks keep working.
Fast. Index and screener rows arrive in seconds; a 50-stock full-profile run finishes in about a minute. Plain HTTP, no browser.
From an AI assistant:* add the MCP connector https://mcp.apify.com/?tools=data_daemon/tickertape-stocks-scraper in Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or VS Code and ask for the data in plain words.

All input fields
FieldTypeMeaning
modestringstocks (default): full profiles for the tickers in stocks. index: all constituents of the index in indexSid. screener: rows matching screenerMatch. Set mode explicitly when you use indexSid or screenerMatch; when it is empty, the mode follows whichever of stocks, screenerMatch or indexSid you filled in.
stocksarrayNSE tickers, company names or Tickertape URLs, e.g. RELIANCE, TCS, Infosys, https://www.tickertape.in/stocks/hdfc-bank-HDBK. Each full profile costs $0.02. Leave empty when you use index or screener mode.
indexSidstringFor index mode. Any index Tickertape lists (77 on 2026-10-18), by name or Tickertape id: NIFTY 50, NIFTY NEXT 50, NIFTY 100, NIFTY 200, NIFTY 500, NIFTY BANK, NIFTY IT, NIFTY AUTO, NIFTY FMCG, NIFTY PHARMA, NIFTY METAL, NIFTY REALTY, NIFTY PSU BANK, NIFTY FIN SERVICE, NIFTY MIDCAP 100, NIFTY MIDCAP 150, NIFTY SMALLCAP 100, NIFTY SMALLCAP 250, SENSEX, BSE 500, or ids such as .NSEI, .NN50, .NIFTYIT. Defaults to NIFTY 50. Each row costs $0.002 (or $0.02 with fullProfile).

Field codes: mrktCapf market cap in ₹ crore, apef P/E, pbr P/B, divYield dividend yield %, roe, roce, dbtEqt debt/equity, pr1w 1-week return %, 4wpct 1-month, 26wpct 6-month, 52wpct 1-year return %, beta, promShrPled pledged promoter %, forInstHldng FII %, domInstHldng DII %, sector (e.g. {"sector": "Energy"}). Each row costs $0.002.

screenerSortDescbooleanSort screener results descending (default) or ascending.
screenerFieldsarrayAdditional Tickertape ratio codes to return per screener row. Every row already carries: subindustry, mrktCapf, lastPrice, apef, pbr, divYield, roe, roce, dbtEqt, pr1w, 4wpct, 26wpct, 52wpct, 52wHigh, 52wLow, beta, promShrPled, forInstHldng, domInstHldng.
fullProfilebooleanFetch the complete profile for every stock ($0.02 each): quote, key ratios, scorecard, 10-year income statement, balance sheet, cash flow, quarterly results, shareholding history, dividends, corporate actions, announcements, analyst forecasts, mutual-fund holders, peers and checklist. Off = lightweight rows ($0.002 each) with price, market cap, P/E, P/B and dividend yield. Defaults to on in stocks mode and off in index / screener mode.
maxItemsintegerStop after this many records (0 = no limit). Useful to cap the cost of a NIFTY 500 or screener run.

Questions buyers ask
How much does it cost to get Indian stock fundamentals?
$0.02 per full stock profile (10 years of statements, quarterly results, shareholding history, dividends, forecasts, peers) and $0.002 per lightweight index or screener row. All of NIFTY 50 with full profiles costs $1.
Which indices are supported?
Any of the 77 indices Tickertape publishes, by name, Tickertape id or index URL: NIFTY 50, NIFTY NEXT 50, NIFTY 100, NIFTY 200, NIFTY 500, NIFTY BANK, NIFTY IT, NIFTY AUTO, NIFTY FMCG, NIFTY PHARMA, NIFTY METAL, NIFTY REALTY, NIFTY PSU BANK, NIFTY FIN SERVICE, NIFTY MIDCAP 100 / 150, NIFTY SMALLCAP 100 / 250, SENSEX, BSE 500 and the other NSE and BSE sector and strategy indices.
What do index rows contain?
Ticker, company name, sector, last price, 1-day change, market cap (₹ crore), P/E, P/B, dividend yield, ROE, 52-week high and low, and free float. Switch on fullProfile for statements, shareholding and forecasts.
Can I run a screener?
Yes. Pass any Tickertape filter object such as {"mrktCapf": {"g": 5000}, "apef": {"l": 20}}. A filter with no matches finishes successfully with 0 rows and a status message.
Does Tickertape have a public API for NSE stock fundamentals?
Tickertape does not publish a documented public API. This Actor reads the data that Tickertape's public stock pages load, without a login, and returns it as JSON: quotes, key ratios, scorecard and 10 years of financial statements for NSE and BSE stocks, plus index member lists. Call it through the Apify API, from Python or Node.js, or from an AI agent, like any Indian stock market API.
Do I need a proxy or login?
No.

Alternatives, honestly
OptionWhat it gives youWhere it falls short for this job

Tickertape website and ProThe same pages for a personNo bulk export or API
Python libraries that read exchange sitesFreeBreak when the exchange changes; fundamentals and shareholding history are thin

# UK Gazette insolvency notices as JSON feed | Daemon Data

Source: https://datadmon.github.io/actors/uk-gazette-insolvency-notices/

UK Gazette insolvency notices as JSON feed

UK Gazette Insolvency Notices Scraper API: Winding-Up Petitions is a pay-per-record Apify Actor by Daemon Data that returns winding-up petitions, administrations, liquidations from The Gazette as JSON, CSV or Excel. It costs $0.005 per notice with the default options ($5.00 per 1,000); no login to the source site and no proxy or browser to set up on your side, and the same input runs from the Apify console, one REST call, Python, Node.js, n8n or an AI assistant through MCP.

Daemon Data UK Gazette Insolvency Notices Scraper API: Winding-Up Petitions on Apify   Listing as plain text

Checked on 17 Oct 2026
In the week of 11 to 17 Oct 2026 The Gazette published 138 winding-up petitions and 43 administration appointments; HMRC presented 56% of the 620 petitions of the prior 30 days. On 21 Oct 2026 the 48-hour corporate-insolvency example returned 100 notices with 98 structured records.

Why teams use it
Structured, joinable fields. Company number for Companies House, postcode, nature of business, petitioner, court, case number, practitioner firm. No copy-pasting notice text.
Earlier than Companies House. Petitions are advertised before the hearing; the company record often changes weeks later.
Any notice type, any date range. Petitions, winding-up orders, administrations, liquidator appointments, creditors' meetings, bankruptcy orders, or personal insolvency.
Built for schedules. publishedWithinDays gives a rolling window, onlyNewSinceLastRun delivers only notices you have not received before, and skipped notices are never charged.
Open Government Licence. Gazette notices are Crown copyright under OGL v3.0; company-level data can be reused with attribution (see "Licence and personal data" below).
From an AI assistant:* add the MCP connector https://mcp.apify.com/?tools=data_daemon/uk-gazette-insolvency-notices in Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or VS Code and ask for the data in plain words.

Output fields
The most useful top-level fields with values from a real record; the full list is noticeId, url, title, category, categories, noticeCode, published, publishedDate, updated, publisher, status, summary, contentHtml, hasDetails, companyNumber, companyName, tradingAs, companyTypes, natureOfBusiness, principalTradingAddress, postcode, courtName, caseNumber, petitioner, petitionerIsHmrc, petitionerAddress, presentedBy, subjectType, dateOfHearing, hearingDate, placeOfHearing, dateOfPetitionPresentation, dateToRequestAppearance, practitioners, practitionerFirm, noticeTypes, linkedData, source, scrapedAt, registeredOffice, courtDistrict, meetingLocation, dateOfAppointment, contactTelephone, contactEmail, previousCompanyName, meetingTime, typeOfLiquidation, dateOfResolution, appointedBy, dateWoundUp. Per-field notes and the OpenAPI definition are on the Apify API page.

All input fields
FieldTypeMeaning
servicestringWhich Gazette search to query. Default insolvency.
noticeTypesarrayOptional Gazette notice type codes (verified Oct 2026): 2450 petitions to wind up (companies), 2451 petitions to wind up (partnerships), 2452 winding-up orders, 2441 resolutions for winding up, 2432 and 2443 appointment of liquidators, 2442 meetings of creditors, 2433 notices to creditors, 2410 appointment of administrators, 2503 bankruptcy orders. Default is petitions and administrations (2450, 2410); pass an empty list for every type in the section.
categoryCodestringOptional Gazette category code, e.g. G205000000 corporate insolvency, G206000000 personal insolvency, G205010000 companies.
textstringOptional free-text search, e.g. Revenue and Customs for HMRC petitions, a company name, a town, or an insolvency practitioner firm.
publishedWithinDaysintegerRelative date window for schedules: only notices published in the last N days, counted back from today (UTC). 1 = since yesterday, 7 = the last week. Ignored when Published from is set. Combine with Only new notices for a daily feed.
startPublishDatestringYYYY-MM-DD. Only notices published on or after this date. Leave empty to use Published within the last N days instead.
endPublishDatestringYYYY-MM-DD. Only notices published on or before this date.
sortBystringSort order. Default latest-date.
includeLinkedDatabooleanFetch each notice's linked-data record and add it as top-level fields: company number, registered office and trading address, postcode, nature of business, petitioner (and an HMRC flag), court and case number, hearing, petition, appointment and resolution dates, and the insolvency practitioner's name, firm, IP number and contact details. Charged as one extra notice-details event per notice where the record was retrieved. Default on.
onlyNewSinceLastRunbooleanDeliver only notices that an earlier run with the same search (or the same State key) has not already delivered. Skipped notices are not charged. Delivered notice ids are remembered for 180 days in a key-value store named uk-gazette-notices-state in your account. Made for daily schedules.
stateNamestringOptional name for this saved search's memory when Only new notices is on. Leave empty to derive it from the section, notice types, category and search text. Use a different key to track several feeds separately.
maxItemsintegerStop after this many notices have been delivered. Default 40, about $0.20 with structured details at FREE prices.

Price
$0.002 per notice ($2.00 per 1,000); $0.003 per notice details ($3.00 per 1,000). List prices for Apify Free and Starter plans; Scale and Business plans pay 15% to 30% less.

Questions buyers ask
How much does it cost to monitor UK winding-up petitions?
$0.002 per notice plus $0.003 for the structured details record. About 140 petitions a week means roughly $3 a month for a daily feed with details.
Does it return only new notices?
Yes. Turn on onlyNewSinceLastRun; each run delivers only notices that earlier runs with the same search have not delivered, and the skipped ones are free.
Can I reuse the data commercially?
Gazette notices are Crown copyright under the Open Government Licence v3.0, so company-level data can be reused with attribution. Personal data is excluded from the licence.
Which notice types are supported?
Any Gazette notice type code. The common corporate ones are 2450 petitions to wind up, 2452 winding-up orders, 2410 appointment of administrators, 2441 resolutions for winding up, 2432 and 2443 appointment of liquidators, 2442 meetings of creditors and 2433 notices to creditors.
Is there a data feed or API for UK winding-up petitions?
The Gazette publishes every insolvency notice in a public feed, with a structured record for each notice, but you have to page the feed, fetch each record and flatten it yourself. This Actor does that and returns one row per notice as JSON, CSV or Excel: company name and number, court and case number, petitioner, petition and hearing dates, practitioners and addresses. With Only new notices and a daily schedule it becomes a winding-up petitions data feed that delivers, and charges for, new notices only.
Do I need a proxy or login?
No. If The Gazette rate-limits the structured-data requests, the Actor switches to Apify datacenter proxy by itself.

Alternatives, honestly
OptionWhat it gives youWhere it falls short for this job
The Gazette website and its paid data serviceOfficial notices; a subscription data service for businessManual reading, or a subscription contract
Companies House APIOfficial company status, freeChanges appear weeks after the petition is advertised
Other Gazette Actors on Apify StoreSame noticesCompare linked-data fields (company number, addresses) and only-new mode

Unstop jobs, internships & hackathons JSON API

Unstop Scraper is a pay-per-record Apify Actor by Daemon Data that returns Unstop jobs, internships, hackathons and competitions with salary or stipend, prizes, deadlines and eligibility as JSON, CSV or Excel. It costs $0.0015 per opportunity with the default options ($1.50 per 1,000); no login to the source site and no proxy or browser to set up on your side, and the same input runs from the Apify console, one REST call, Python, Node.js, n8n or an AI assistant through MCP.

Daemon Data Unstop Scraper on Apify   Listing as plain text

Checked on 30 Oct 2026
the default run (50 newest jobs + 50 newest internships with descriptions) took 7 seconds on the Apify platform and cost $0.15 plus the $0.001 start fee. 81 of the 100 were paid, 42 showed a salary or stipend figure, 26 were work from home and 49 were open to freshers; every listing had been posted the day before. On 26 Oct 2026, 137 jobs had been posted in the last 3 days, 47 of them in Bangalore or remote; 60 open jobs and 309 internships were work from home, 146 internships were unpaid, and 89 hackathons were offline (in person). All input fields
FieldTypeMeaning
opportunityTypesarrayUnstop listing types. Each type is one search; a listing is saved and charged once. On 30 Oct 2026 Unstop had about 880 open jobs, 590 internships, 400 competitions, 190 hackathons, 100 workshops, 80 quizzes and 6 scholarships.
searchTermsarrayOptional. Unstop matches them against listing titles and organisation names, e.g. data analyst, marketing, software engineer, Reliance. Each keyword runs once per type. Leave empty to get every open listing of the chosen types.
workplaceTypesarrayOnly jobs and internships with these workplace types. Empty = any.
timingstringOnly full-time or only part-time jobs and internships.
paystringMostly useful for internships: paid (with a stipend) or unpaid.
eligibilitystringOnly listings open to this group, as set by the organiser.
modestringOnly online or only in-person events.
entryFeestringOnly free or only paid-entry events.
postedWithinDaysintegerOnly listings published on Unstop in the last N days (e.g. 1 for a daily feed, 7 for weekly). 0 or empty = any date.
locationsarrayOnly listings whose city, state or country contains one of these words, e.g. Bangalore, Mumbai, Maharashtra. remote matches work-from-home jobs. Listings without a location (many online events) are left out when this is set.
includeDescriptionbooleanFull description as plain text (description) and HTML (descriptionHtml). It costs the same either way; turn it off for smaller files.
maxResultsPerSearchintegerCap for each type (and keyword). Newest listings come first. 0 = no cap: every open listing, about 2,350 across all types.
maxResultsintegerStop after this many saved listings. 0 or empty = no total cap (the run's maximum cost still applies).
onlyNewSinceLastRunbooleanFor schedules: remember delivered listing ids (in a named key-value store in your account) and save only listings that earlier runs with the same settings did not deliver. Skipped listings are not charged.
stateNamestringName of the only-new memory. Empty = derived from the types, keywords and filters. Give two schedules the same name to share one memory.
skipIdsarrayUnstop listing ids you already have (the id field). They are neither saved nor charged.

Price
$0.0015 per opportunity ($1.50 per 1,000); $0.001 per run. List prices for Apify Free and Starter plans; Scale and Business plans pay 15% to 30% less.
EventPricePer 1,000Charged when
Opportunity$0.0015$1.50One Unstop listing saved to the dataset (job, internship, hackathon, competition, quiz, workshop or scholarship): id, URL, title, organiser, locations, workplace type, salary or stipend, eligibility, skills, registration dates and deadline, team size, entry fee, prizes, registration and view counts, and the full description (text + HTML). Skipped or filtered listings are never charged.
Actor Start$0.001Charged when the Actor starts running. Number of events charged depends on Actor memory (one event per GB, minimum one event).
Cost example: 50 opportunitys with default options cost $0.076, including any start fee. This is an illustrative record count; set explicit row and total-charge caps for your run. Saved inputs you can run with one click on Apify (Examples tab); each has its own page:

Questions buyers ask
Is there an official Unstop API?
Unstop does not offer a documented public API. This Actor reads the public JSON endpoints (/api/public/opportunity/...) that the unstop.com website loads, which robots.txt allows. It exposes them as a REST API with schedules, webhooks and only-new runs, so you do not maintain a scraper or proxies yourself.
How much does it cost to scrape Unstop?
$0.0015 per listing with its description plus $0.001 per run, so 100 listings cost about $0.15, every open hackathon and competition about $0.90, and a weekly only-new hackathon digest about $0.33 a month.
Is it legal to scrape Unstop?
The Actor only reads listings that Unstop shows to anyone without a login, through endpoints its robots.txt allows, and it collects no data about candidates or participants. Public listing data is generally collected for aggregation, research and recruiting; you remain responsible for complying with Unstop's terms of use and the law that applies to you.
Can I get a list of all open hackathons on Unstop?
Yes: opportunityTypes: ["hackathons"] with maxResultsPerSearch: 0 returns every hackathon open for registration (193 on 30 Oct 2026), with organiser, mode, team size, prizes and deadline. Add competitions for case-study challenges and other contests. The open hackathons example runs it with one click.
Can I export Unstop listings to Excel or Google Sheets?
Yes. Every run's dataset downloads as CSV, Excel, JSON, XML or HTML, and the task's Integrations tab appends rows to a Google Sheet after each run.
Does it return closed listings?
No. It returns listings that are open for registration, which is what Unstop shows by default.
Does it include participants or applicant details?
No. It returns listing data only: the organiser, the role or event, deadlines and counts. No personal data about candidates or participants is collected.
Why does a salary show as empty?
The organiser chose not to show a figure. On the 30 Oct 2026 default run 81 of 100 jobs and internships were paid and 42 showed a salary or stipend amount; paid tells you which unpaid ones to skip.

Checked on 30 Oct 2026

One HTTP call starts a run, waits for it and returns the records (token from console.apify.com):

curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/data_daemon~welcome-to-the-jungle-jobs-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"queries": ["python"], "countryCodes": ["FR"], "contractTypes": ["FULL_TIME"], "maxJobs": 20}'

Python: ApifyClient(token).actor("data_daemon/welcome-to-the-jungle-jobs-scraper").call(run_input=...). Python example · Node.js example · n8n workflow.
AI assistant (MCP): add the remote server https://mcp.apify.com/?tools=data_daemon/welcome-to-the-jungle-jobs-scraper with header Authorization: Bearer YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN in Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or VS Code and ask for the data in plain words.

All input fields
FieldTypeMeaning
queriesarrayOne public WTTJ search per keyword; jobs shared by several searches are delivered once. Default: python. An empty array runs no searches. Maximum 50 searches.
countryCodesarrayOptional two-letter office country codes, for example FR, ES or DE. Several values match any of them. Covers the France-focused public WTTJ board, including its jobs abroad; not the separate Otta/US/UK matching inventory.
locationsarrayOptional case-insensitive substring match on public office city, region or country. Accents are ignored. Several values match any of them. Applied locally within the source search window; use countryCodes to narrow the source search first.
contractTypesarrayOptional: FULL_TIME, TEMPORARY, INTERNSHIP, APPRENTICESHIP, FREELANCE, VIE, PART_TIME or OTHER. Several values match any of them; other filter groups are combined with AND.
remoteModesarrayOptional: fulltime (fully remote), partial (hybrid), punctual (occasional), no or unknown. Several values match any of them. This is the source designation, not a promise that applicants can work from any country.
languagesarrayOptional two-letter posting language codes such as fr or en. Several values match any of them.
companySlugsarrayOptional company URL slugs, for example webnet or elis-france. Several values match any of them. These must be slugs, not display names.
salaryCurrencystringOptional three-letter currency such as EUR. Filters on disclosed currency, not salary size. Salary numbers are preserved as provided; employers use inconsistent units.
postedWithinDaysintegerOptional 1-365 day posting window; 0 means no date filter. Jobs with unknown dates are excluded when enabled. Applied locally before fetching descriptions.
includeDescriptionbooleanRead each public job detail endpoint for description HTML, plain text, candidate profile, recruitment process and public company metadata. Off returns search listing data only. Same price per delivered job.
maxJobsPerQueryintegerMaximum delivered jobs per keyword, after filters and exclusions. Default 20. 0 means up to the source maximum of 1,000 accessible hits per search. Narrow broad searches with country/company/contract filters.
maxJobsintegerGlobal delivery cap across keywords. Default 20; 0 removes this cap but the per-keyword and 1,000-hit source windows still apply. Set a maximum charge in Apify for a spending cap.
skipJobIdsarrayOptional output id, sourceId or dedupKey values. Excluded jobs are skipped before detail requests and are not charged. Suitable for a database or spreadsheet containing jobs you already have.
onlyNewSinceLastRunbooleanRemember delivered job IDs in a persistent named key-value store. Later runs with the same state name return unseen jobs. Skipped jobs are not charged. First run is a baseline capped by maxJobs; later runs may fill older unseen backlog. Memory expires after 120 days and retains at most 50,000 IDs per feed.
stateNamestringOptional stable name for an only-new feed (maximum 120 characters). Same name shares memory across tasks in your account; avoid overlapping runs. Leave empty to derive a name from the search filters. Change the name for a fresh baseline.

Price
$0.0008 per job ($0.80 per 1,000); $0.001 per run. List prices for Apify Free and Starter plans; Scale and Business plans pay 15% to 30% less.
EventPricePer 1,000Charged when
Job$0.0008$0.80One delivered public WTTJ job: full description when enabled, company profile, offices, contract and remote labels, disclosed salary as provided.
Actor Start$0.001Charged when the Actor starts running. Number of events charged depends on Actor memory (one event per GB, minimum one event).
Cost example: 20 jobs with default options cost $0.017, including any start fee. This is an illustrative record count; set explicit row and total-charge caps for your run. Apify's free plan includes $5 of usage a month, about 6,250 jobs before start fees; the Actor's own compute is included in the per-record price, and records skipped by filters, de-duplication or only-new mode are not charged.

What it is not for
Separate Otta/US/UK personalized matching inventory; normalized salary benchmarks (raw source units vary); more than 1,000 hits per source search. The data belongs to its publisher; the Actor reads public pages and endpoints and leaves out personal contact details.

Questions buyers ask
Is there an official Welcome to the Jungle API?
Welcome to the Jungle does not publish a public jobs API for third parties. This Actor reads the public search index and job detail endpoints that the welcometothejungle.com site itself loads and exposes them as a REST API with schedules, webhooks and only-new feeds, so you do not maintain a scraper yourself.
Is it legal to scrape Welcome to the Jungle?
The Actor only reads job and company information that the site shows to anyone without an account, and it collects no applicant data or private recruiter contact details. Public job data is generally collected for aggregation, research and recruiting; you remain responsible for complying with Welcome to the Jungle's terms of use and the data-protection law (including the GDPR) that applies to you.
Can I export Welcome to the Jungle jobs to Excel or Google Sheets?
Yes. Every run's dataset downloads as CSV, Excel, JSON, XML or HTML, and the task's Integrations tab appends rows to a Google Sheet after each run.

minAreaintegerKeep listings with at least this usable area.

includeImagesbooleanUp to 10 photo URLs per listing in imageUrls.
maxResultsPerSearchintegerCap per location (and neighborhood). 0 = no cap. Searches with more than ~1,000 listings are split into price bands automatically.
maxResultsintegerStop after this many saved listings (default 50, about $0.05). 0 = no cap (the run's maximum cost still applies).
onlyNewSinceLastRunbooleanRemember delivered listing ids in a key-value store named zap-vivareal-state in your account and skip them next time (not charged). Use with a schedule for a daily new-listings feed.
stateNamestringName of the only-new memory. By default it follows portals, sale/rent, locations and neighborhoods, so different feeds don't mix.
skipIdsarrayListing ids you already have. They are neither saved nor charged.

# Dubai Land Department transactions as JSON: registered sold prices, weekly volumes and how to pull them

Source: https://datadmon.github.io/guides/dubai-land-department-transactions-json/

The Dubai Land Department (DLD) publishes every registered property transaction in Dubai as open data: each sale, off-plan pre-registration, mortgage registration and gift, with the transaction date, the value in AED, the area and project, property type, rooms, parking and size. It is the only source of **actual registered prices** for Dubai; listing portals show asking prices. This guide explains what the register contains, how much data it produces and how to pull it as JSON.

## What a week of DLD data looks like (measured 11 to 18 October 2026)

| Transaction group | Transactions per week | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Sales | about 2,600 | 1,650 off-plan (developer pre-registrations), 950 ready properties |
| Mortgages | about 1,300 | registrations and modifications, separated by the `procedure` field |
| Gifts | about 160 | transfers between family members |
| Land plots | about 220 of the sales | `propertyType: "land"` |
| **Total** | **about 4,100** | a typical week is 3,000 to 6,000 |

Roughly 2,500 of the 2,600 weekly sales are residential; the rest are commercial.

## Fields in each record

Every record carries the transaction date (ISO), transaction number, `procedure` (for example `Sale`, `Delayed Sell`, `Sell - Pre registration`, mortgage registration or modification), transaction group, property type and sub-type, usage (residential or commercial), area and project names (a master project only on the rare rows where DLD names one, under 1%), rooms, parking, actual area in square metres, value in AED and a precomputed `pricePerSqmAed`, plus boolean off-plan and freehold flags. Arabic names are available as an optional object. The register contains no owner names or contact details.

## Free portals versus the register as data

Dubai Pulse (the government open-data portal) and DXB Interact (DLD's dashboard) let you look up transactions and download extracts by hand. They are the right tools for a one-off question. They are the wrong tools for a daily feed into a database, a valuation model that needs price per square metre by project, or an app that shows registered prices next to listings, because each extract is manual and the files need cleaning. The Daemon Data API reads the same DLD open-data service, pages through the whole date range 500 rows at a time and returns analysis-ready records.

## How to pull it

One call returns last week's residential unit sales (about 2,500 rows, about $2.50):

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/data_daemon~dubai-property-transactions/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"daysBack": 7, "transactionGroup": "sales", "usage": "residential", "propertyType": "unit", "maxItems": 0}'
```

For a daily feed, save the input with `daysBack: 1` as a task and schedule it; the ready-made example page "Dubai DLD property transactions, last 24 hours, as JSON" returned 1,000 transactions in 6 seconds on 21 October 2026. For a date range use `fromDate` and `toDate` (`YYYY-MM-DD`). To filter by area, read the `area` and `project` fields of the output; the service's own area id filter returns no rows at present.

## What it costs

$1 per 1,000 transactions, nothing else. A month of all sales (about 11,000 rows) costs about $11; a weekly residential feed about $2.50 a week; a daily feed of everything about $17 a month. Apify's free plan includes $5 of usage every month.

## Questions and answers

**Is this official Dubai Land Department data?**

Yes. The API reads the Dubai Land Department's own open-data transactions service, the same register that paid DLD data products resell. It is published by the department for reuse.

**Are these asking prices or sold prices?**

Registered transaction values, that is what buyers actually paid or what was registered for a mortgage or gift. Asking prices come from listing portals and are not in the register.

**How do I tell an off-plan pre-registration from a completed sale?**

Use the `procedure` field: `Sell - Pre registration` is a developer pre-registration, `Sale` and `Delayed Sell` are completed sales. The `offPlan` input filter and the boolean flag in each record do the same split.

**Does the register include owner names?**

No. The open-data service carries no personal data, and the API adds none.

**How far back can I go?**

Any date range the DLD service holds; the input accepts `fromDate` and `toDate`, or `daysBack` up to 365.

# How to export every IIMJobs and Hirist job as a daily feed

Source: https://datadmon.github.io/guides/iimjobs-hirist-full-board-job-feed/

Job aggregators, HR-tech products and hiring-market trackers usually need **all** of a job board, not the results of a few keywords. IIMJobs.com (MBA, finance, consulting, sales, HR and senior management roles in India) and Hirist.tech (India's tech-only board) have no public export. Since 26 October 2026 the **IIMJobs Jobs Scraper** and the **Hirist.tech Jobs Scraper** on Apify can deliver every listing a board shows in a date window, with the same fields as a keyword search.

## How much there is

Measured on 26 October 2026 with the boards' own date filters:

| Board | Jobs posted in the last 7 days | Last 30 days |
|---|---:|---:|
| IIMJobs | 1,199 (about 170 a day) | 4,602 |
| Hirist | 959 (about 140 a day) | 4,448 |

Weekends are quieter: on a Sunday IIMJobs showed 17 new listings.

## Step 1: run the full board once

Open the [IIMJobs Jobs Scraper](https://apify.com/data_daemon/iimjobs-jobs-scraper) (or the [Hirist.tech Jobs Scraper](https://apify.com/data_daemon/hirist-jobs-scraper)), switch on **All jobs on the board** and run it with:

```json
{
  "allJobs": true,
  "postedWithinDays": 3,
  "onlyNewSinceLastRun": true,
  "stateName": "iimjobs-full-board"
}
```

The Actor ignores the keywords and walks every listing posted in the window, newest first. Each row has the job ID, title, company (with industry, size and AmbitionBox rating when available), locations, experience range, salary in LPA when disclosed, skills, applicant and view counts, posting time and the full job description. `locations`, the experience range and `maxJobs` still apply if you only want part of the board. Putting `*` in the keywords does the same as the switch.

## Step 2: schedule it daily

Create a daily Apify schedule for the run (or a saved task with this input). Because of **only-new mode**, every later run returns only jobs the feed named by `stateName` has not delivered yet; repeats are skipped and not charged. We checked this on 26 October 2026: two back-to-back runs returned 15 and then 2 jobs, with no job delivered twice.

The date window counts calendar days in India time. Three days is a safe window for a daily schedule: it covers weekends and a run that starts late, and only-new mode removes the overlap.

## Step 3: load it where you need it

The dataset of each run is available as JSON, CSV or Excel through the Apify API, so a database loader, an n8n or Make workflow, or a Google Sheets import can pick it up. Key on `dedupKey` (for example `iimjobs:1741775`), which is stable across runs and boards.

## The same switch on Foundit and Instahyre

The [Foundit Jobs Scraper](https://apify.com/data_daemon/foundit-jobs-scraper) and the [Instahyre Jobs Scraper](https://apify.com/data_daemon/instahyre-jobs-scraper) have the same **All jobs on the board** option. foundit (formerly Monster India) is far busier: **2,815 jobs posted in the last day** on 26 October 2026, so its window defaults to one day. Instahyre had **12,724 open jobs** and no date filter on the site, so follow it with only-new mode alone: the first run exports the open jobs (about 80 minutes at roughly three jobs a second; it stops cleanly before the run timeout and the next run continues), and later runs return only jobs that are new to the feed.

## Costs and limits

Each Actor charges per job saved, with the price shown on its Apify pricing tab; jobs skipped by only-new mode are free. A board-wide daily feed is roughly the number of new jobs per day from the table above. Set **Maximum cost per run** on the schedule if you want a hard ceiling; the run stops cleanly at that limit and says so.

# How to get new IIMJobs postings in Google Sheets every morning

Source: https://datadmon.github.io/guides/iimjobs-new-jobs-google-sheets/

Recruiters, career coaches and hiring-market analysts who follow **IIMJobs.com** usually want one thing: the jobs that appeared since yesterday, in a spreadsheet, without copying them by hand and without seeing the same posting twice. IIMJobs has no public API or export, so this guide sets up a daily feed with the **IIMJobs Jobs Scraper** on Apify and a free n8n workflow that writes the rows to Google Sheets and posts a summary to Slack.

## What you get in each row

Every job comes back as one row with the job ID, title, company (name, industry, size and AmbitionBox rating when available), locations, experience range, salary in LPA when the recruiter discloses it, skills, applicant count, posting date, the public job URL and, if you switch it on, the full job description. Most IIMJobs recruiters hide pay, so a `salaryHidden` flag tells you which rows have none.

Demand is large enough to make a feed worthwhile: a `product manager` search matched 4,097 open IIMJobs listings and `investment banking` 652 when we measured them between 18 and 21 October 2026.

## Step 1: run the Actor once with only-new mode

Open the [IIMJobs Jobs Scraper on Apify](https://apify.com/data_daemon/iimjobs-jobs-scraper), click **Try for free** and paste this input:

```json
{
  "queries": ["product manager", "investment banking"],
  "onlyNewSinceLastRun": true,
  "stateName": "my-daily-feed",
  "maxJobs": 100
}
```

`onlyNewSinceLastRun` makes the Actor remember which job IDs this feed (named by `stateName`) has already delivered. The next run returns only jobs it has not sent before, and **skipped repeats are not charged**. We checked this on 23 October 2026: two back-to-back runs with the same feed name returned six different jobs and no repeats.

## Step 2: schedule it

In Apify Console open **Schedules**, create a daily schedule (for example 08:00 in Asia/Kolkata) and add the Actor run or a saved task with the input above. Each morning the dataset of that run contains only the new postings.

## Step 3: send the rows to Google Sheets and Slack with n8n

If you use [n8n](https://n8n.io), import the ready workflow [iimjobs-new-jobs-to-google-sheets-and-slack.json](https://github.com/datadmon/apify-data-actors-examples/blob/main/n8n/iimjobs-new-jobs-to-google-sheets-and-slack.json). It runs at 08:00, calls the Actor through the Apify API with only-new mode, **upserts** each job into a `Jobs` tab (matched on `id`, so re-runs never duplicate rows) and posts the count and the first five jobs to a Slack channel. Setup:

1. Create an n8n *Header Auth* credential named `Authorization` with the value `Bearer YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN` (Apify Console → Settings → API & Integrations).
2. Connect Google Sheets and paste your sheet URL. Add a `Jobs` tab with the header row `id, title, company, locations, experience, salaryLpa, skills, applicants, postedAt, url`.
3. Connect Slack, pick a channel, edit the `queries` and activate the workflow.

The request URL already carries `maxTotalChargeUsd=0.5`, a hard cost cap per run.

Prefer code? The same feed is a few lines of Python with the official `apify-client` package; a complete example is in the [examples repository](https://github.com/datadmon/apify-data-actors-examples/tree/main/examples/only-new-jobs).

## Tips

- **One feed per question.** Use a separate `stateName` for each search you track, for example `pm-mumbai` and `ib-all-india`. Changing the queries under the same name mixes their memory.
- **Narrow the first run.** The first run delivers a capped baseline of open jobs; later runs add only the new ones. Add `"postedWithinDays": 1` if you never want older postings.
- **Tech roles instead?** Point the same workflow at `data_daemon~hirist-jobs-scraper`; the input and output fields are the same.
- **Cost.** Both Actors are pay-per-result with a free trial; the current price is on each Apify page.

## FAQ

**Is there an official IIMJobs API?** No public one. The Actor reads the job data the IIMJobs website itself loads, needs no login, cookies or proxy, and returns it as JSON, CSV, Excel or rows in your sheet.

**Does it collect recruiter contact details?** No. Recruiter names and phone numbers are left out on purpose; the recruiter's designation is kept only where IIMJobs shows it to every visitor.

**Can I get alerts in Microsoft Teams or email instead of Slack?** Yes: replace the Slack node in n8n with a Teams or Gmail node. Make and Zapier can call the same Apify Actor as well.
